newsitem.title: EGYPT: RESEARCH ALERT - Technopack starts as "strong buy".
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Technopack starts as "strong buy".

text.p: London-based stockbrokers T. Hoare and Co said on Tuesday it was giving an initial "strong buy" rating to Egyptian packaging company Technopack.

It said that with 65 percent of the Egyptian packaging market and as the biggest company of its kind in all Africa, the company was well placed to take advantage of a domestic packaging market that could grow 200 percent in five years.

It estimated that Technopack's net profits would increase from 10.660 million pounds in calendar 1996 to 14.970 million in 1997, 20.969 million in 1998, 34.951 million in 1999 and 48.557 million in the year 2000.
The company's shares last traded at 37.00 pounds -- giving an estimated price/earnings ratio of about 11.4. The company has 4.6 million issued shares.

"Consumer lifestyles in Egypt are changing...towards the establishment of supermarkets, fast food and packaged products. The high demand for packaging-related new applications will continue to play into the hands of the market leader," the T. Hoare research alert said.
Technopack has capacity to produce 10,000 tonnes a year of BOPP (biaxially oriented polypropylene packaging) and has plans to double capacity to 20,000 tonnes a year.

"A recent independent survey estimates the size of the domestic market (for BOPP) will increase to 20,000 tonnes a year by 2001, currently 11,100 tonnes a year. This provides the market leader...with a large untapped market," it said.
Technopack is doing feasibility studies to enter the converter or packaging printing industry. The report said that by doing so the company would dramatically improve its margins.
T. Hoare has a strategic alliance with Triple A Securities, one of Egypt's biggest stockbrokers.
